text:
oncall-bot: Paging @eng-oncall: sudden p95 latency + increased 5xx on runtime-prod (us-east-1) for /v1/generate. Canary 10% shows tail latency spike ~600ms -> 2.1s since 02:15 UTC. Alert: runtime-latency-sla-breach.
jamal: seeing it, joining. which release rolled?
svetlana: rollout: release/2026-03-17-batching-optimizations -> canary 10% started 02:12 UTC, tag: v2.14.3. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/864
eli: adding traces. cb: kernel fallback events spiking on inference nodes (KV cache miss growth). logs: `kernel_fallback=true` in runtime logs.
mike: canaries look noisy but 1% traffic still ok. ops-bot: autoscaler didn't trigger extra pods due to throttle cap.
jamal: @eli paste the minimal logs/snippet pls
eli:```\n[02:14:37] node-17 runtime: batch_scheduler: prefetch_queue len=2300\n[02:14:38] node-17 runtime: kv_cache_miss=0.62 rate/s\n[02:14:38] node-17 runtime: kernel_fallback=true reason=quant_kernel_error\n[02:14:39] node-17 runtime: rt_latency_p95=2100ms\n```\nsvetlana: I think the new prefetch heuristics increased concurrent prefetch streams -> IO thrash -> kernel fallback and degraded batching.
jamal: @svetlana can we flip the feature flag for canary only? What's the kill-switch name?
svetlana: flag: `prefetch.experimental_streaming` - rollout was enabled at 100% for the new runtime variant, but canary nodes got the variant first.
mike: command to disable in prod: `/ops/feature-flag set prefetch.experimental_streaming=false --env=prod --target=canary` (ops runbook)
jamal: I will coordinate. Eli, can you prepare rollback plan if flag flip doesn't reduce errors?
eli: onboard: rollback path = revert rollout to previous runtime variant via deployment rollback (kubectl rollout undo) + scale up old-pool. Will need ~6-8 mins to ramp.
oncall-bot: Incident severity: Sev2. Paging escalation policy triggered.
svetlana: flipping flag now on canary nodes only.
jamal: `opsbot: run feature-flag disable prefetch.experimental_streaming --scope=canary --initiator=jamal`
ops-bot: Executing: feature-flag disable prefetch.experimental_streaming scope=canary initiator=jamal
ops-bot: Done. 6/6 canary nodes updated.
mike: metrics watch: p95 dropping from 2.1s -> 820ms in first 90s on updated canaries. 5xx rate trending down. :thumbsup:
eli: tracing confirms reduced kernel_fallback events on nodes with flag off.
svetlana: good. roll forward to full rollout pause? I'm recommending pause the deployment and keep flag off until we validate on 30% traffic.
jamal: agreed. Pausing rollout and tagging release for rollback readiness.
customer-success: heads up: we saw 2 customer reports of lag during the spike. I'm drafting an incident notice for impacted tenants.
mike: can we confirm which customers hit the canary nodes? csv of request ids matched to accounts available. Eli will share.
eli: shared list to #support-private. minimal customer impact: 2 customers saw degraded responses for ~3-8 minutes, no data loss.
jamal: handoff: I'll stay until metrics stable for 30m. Next oncall @svetlana will take after. Please add postmortem stub.
svetlana: noted. Postmortem tags: regression, prefetch, kernel-fallback, feature-flag, rollout.
oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: next_oncall=svetlana at 03:10 UTC.
jamal: quick root cause hypothesis: new prefetch streaming increased I/O concurrency leading to slower KV reads, triggering quantized kernel fallback and higher latency. Mitigation: revert heuristics + rate-limit prefetch streams and harden kernel fallback path.
mike: action items: 1) keep rollout paused; 2) revert heuristics in next patch or gate via flag; 3) add canary-only throttle in autoscaler to avoid underprovision; 4) postmortem + customer comms.
customer-success: will send customer note summarizing duration and mitigation.
eli: I'll prepare a small perf test to replicate locally and validate fix before re-enabling flag. ETA 4h.
jamal: thanks everyone. I'll update #incidents with final summary once we complete 30m stable window. :white_check_mark:
